name: Jobs & Projects portal (tabbed hub)
purpose: One page holding six tabs: Jobs, Projects, Field data, Activity, Weather, Compliance. It replaced seven separate sidebar pages in the 2026-08-24 consolidation.

elements.name: Tab strip (Jobs / Projects / Field data / Activity / Weather / Compliance)
elements.does: Selects the panel via ?tab=. Only the active panel mounts, so a tab fetches only when opened.

elements.name: New job / Import buttons
elements.does: Shown to admins on the Jobs tab only. Link to /admin/jobs/new and /admin/jobs/import.

elements.name: New Project button
elements.does: Shown to admins on the Projects tab only. Links to /admin/projects/new.

elements.name: Per-tab hint line
elements.does: One sentence under the tabs describing the active tab.

behaviours: Default tab is Projects, not Jobs (page.tsx:87), although the page and route are called Jobs.
Tabs are filtered per viewer role; if every tab is switched off for the firm the page shows a 'switched off for this company' message (page.tsx:~105).
Old routes /admin/projects, /timeline, /field-data, /weather, /vehicles, /schedule forward here with ?tab= so bookmarks survive.
problems: Two of the six tabs (Weather, Compliance) are not jobs or projects at all; 'Field data' and 'Activity' are about people and devices rather than jobs. The tab strip is a junk drawer for 'things office people look at'.

The Activity tab hint promises 'what the firm did today: clock-ins, stage changes, uploads', but the tab renders the per-user Daily Timeline of GPS stops (see jobs.activity-timeline). The hint and the page disagree.
Defaulting to Projects while the nav and URL say Jobs makes first-time users hunt for the job list.
File headers in app/admin/jobs/_tabs/* still carry the old route's comment (e.g. ActivityTab says 'app/admin/timeline/page.tsx'), which makes the code hard to navigate.
rebuild: Make /admin/jobs a single work board: Jobs (default) and Projects as two views of the same list with a grouping toggle, plus a 'Today' view for the crew calendar. Move Weather into the schedule/calendar day view, Compliance into Company settings, and Field data into each job's Field panel plus one office inbox of unreviewed uploads.
add: Saved filters and a 'my jobs' view
nationwide: No Starr-specific content. Tab visibility and roles are per-firm settings already (Settings → Pages). Role names (admin/developer/tech_support/field_crew) need mapping to a firm's own roles.

name: All Jobs list (Jobs tab)
purpose: Browse and search every job, by stage, as cards or a list.

elements.name: Search box
elements.does: Server-side ilike on name, job number, client name and address (route.ts:88).

elements.name: Stage pipeline strip
elements.does: Counts per stage (quote, research, fieldwork, drawing, legal, delivery, completed); click to filter. Cancelled and on-hold are hidden from it (JobsTab.tsx:238).

elements.name: Grid / List toggle
elements.does: Switches between card grid and table list.

elements.name: Deleted view
elements.does: Shows soft-deleted jobs; Delete moves a job to a 30-day recycle bin, Restore PUTs deleted_at:null.

elements.name: New badge
elements.does: Marks jobs this person has not opened yet, from the unread job_created notification.

behaviours: Delete is a soft delete with 30-day recovery (route.ts:432).
A job card shows number, stage chip, deadline bubble, team count and tags.
The stage description tooltips in this file explain each stage in surveying terms.
problems: No column sort, no assignee or due-date filter, no 'overdue' or 'mine' view: a firm with 200 open jobs cannot triage from here.
Stage is the only axis; on_hold and cancelled are hidden from the strip even though they are stored in the same stage column.
Stage descriptions are duplicated here and in STAGE_CONFIG; both hard-code the Starr seven-stage flow.
rebuild: One dense table (job number, client, site, type, status, assigned PM, party chief, due date, % billed) with saved views and a board view. Status chips come from the canonical lifecycle in jobs.md.
nationwide: Stage names and the tooltips that describe them are Starr's workflow. They must come from a per-firm pipeline config.

name: New job form
purpose: Create a job inside a project, optionally converting a lead (?fromLead=) and pre-filling from it.

elements.name: Project picker (required)
elements.does: Chooses the parent project; ?project= preselects it. Client and site are inherited from the project once, at creation.

elements.name: Client, property, legal-description fields
elements.does: Name, address with Google autocomplete, county, abstract number (GLO), lot, acreage.

elements.name: Lead RPLS email, deadline, tags, quote amount, stage
elements.does: Stored on the job. Stage defaults to 'quote'.

elements.name: Job number field
elements.does: Optional; the API generates YYYY-NNN when blank.

behaviours: With ?fromLead=<id> the form prefills from the lead (buildJobDraftFromLead), then after create PATCHes the lead to status 'accepted' and stamps converted_job_id (best-effort; failure is only logged) (page.tsx:218-232).
The API refuses a job with no project_id (route.ts:148). Job number is MAX-based per org per year (route.ts:199-210).
Creating a job writes a stage history row, an activity_log row and a job_created notification to the team.
problems: Converting a lead marks it 'accepted' at the moment the job is created, but the job starts in the 'quote' stage with the checklist item 'Quote accepted by client'. 'Accepted' is therefore stated twice and the two can disagree.
A job number is burned for every quote, including those that are lost. Firms normally number the job when the work is won, and number proposals separately.
Lead conversion is a best-effort second request: if it fails, the lead stays 'new' with a job already created (duplicate follow-up risk).
Single long form: 600+ lines of fields for a firm that would enter client, site, type, and due date and fill the rest later.
rebuild: A two-step 'New job' dialog: pick or create the project (client + site), then job type, scope, due date and fee. Lead conversion becomes one server transaction (lead to won, project created, job created, quote copied as the fee). Job numbers are assigned when a quote is accepted.
add: Job templates by type (boundary, topo, ALTA, stakeout, elevation certificate) with default scope, checklist and fee
Fee schedule or lump-sum vs hourly flag
Duplicate-job detection by address or parcel
nationwide: biasTexas autocomplete (page.tsx:463), 'Texas GLO abstract number' tooltip (page.tsx:536), TBPELS-flavoured RPLS wording. Parcel identifier needs to be a per-state field set (abstract number, PIN, APN, section-township-range). 'RPLS' is a Texas licence title; make it 'responsible licensed surveyor'.

name: Import legacy jobs and files
purpose: Bring historical jobs in from a CSV, and upload files against them.

elements.name: CSV drop and preview
elements.does: Parses client-side (parseCSVLine, page.tsx:~133), shows headers and rows.

elements.name: Column mapping
elements.does: Maps CSV columns to job fields before submit.

elements.name: File upload step
elements.does: Posts to /api/admin/jobs/files.

behaviours: Posts rows one by one to /api/admin/jobs.
Each imported job needs a project; the page must pick or create one.
problems: Not verified end to end: it was written before projects became mandatory, and whether it creates projects per row is not confirmed in the code read.
Hand-rolled CSV parser instead of a library; quoted-newline cases are untested.
rebuild: A first-run migration wizard: upload a spreadsheet or QuickBooks/Jobber/Monday export, map columns, group rows into projects by client + site, preview, and import in one transaction with an undo.
add: Importers for common firm tools (QuickBooks, Smartsheet, Excel templates)
nationwide: Import mapping must be configurable; firms arrive with their own spreadsheets and numbering.

name: Job detail workspace (7 tabs)
purpose: The single page a job is run from: overview, scheduling, files, field work, property map, financial, activity, messages.

elements.name: Header: stage badge, Export PDF, result control
elements.does: Shows stage; exports a one-page client-side PDF summary; sets won/lost/abandoned with reason.

elements.name: Stage timeline
elements.does: JobStageTimeline: click a stage to move there (both directions); opening a stage also jumps to its folder.

elements.name: Action row
elements.does: Upload files, Files and photos, Interactive map, View field captures, Delete job.

elements.name: Overview tab
elements.does: Originating inquiry card, research packet, property panel, inline-editable client, deliverables, team, equipment, checklist.

elements.name: Schedule tab
elements.does: Three-phase scheduler (Research, Field, Drawing and Deliverables) plus job instructions.

elements.name: Files tab
elements.does: One folder explorer (Research, CAD, Photos, Videos, Documents) replacing five older tabs.

elements.name: Field Work tab
elements.does: Job notes, field media panel and FieldWorkView (collector points plot).

elements.name: Property Map tab
elements.does: Summary and entry to /admin/map?job=.

elements.name: Financial tab
elements.does: JobMoneyPanel and JobTimeTracker.

elements.name: Activity / Messages tabs
elements.does: Job activity feed; per-job conversation embedded from messaging.

behaviours: 1,446-line client component; loads the job, stage history, checklists, team, equipment in separate calls.
Opening the page POSTs /api/admin/jobs/[id]/open so recently viewed jobs sort first, and clears the 'New' badge.
Old tab keys (research, cad, photos, videos) are remapped to Files folders (page.tsx:~284 openTab).
Inline edits save field by field through PUT /api/admin/jobs.
problems: Three tabs and two buttons all lead to 'what the crew captured': Field Work tab, Property Map tab, the 'Interactive map' button, 'View field captures', and the Files > Photos folder. Same point, five doors.
'Field Work' is the name of a stage, a tab, and a legacy component (FieldWorkView) over a table (job_field_data) that holds zero rows per the 2026-09-20 review.
Deliverables is a free-text field here; the real deliverable records (revision, seal, issued-to) have an API and no screen (see jobs.deliverables-api).
No change-order, proposal or invoice panel on the job, even though the data and API exist.
Overview tab is long: nine panels stacked, no 'what needs doing next' summary beyond the checklist.
Page is one 1,446-line file with its own copies of types and tab logic; hard to change safely.
rebuild: Job page = header (number, client, site, status, PM, due date, fee and billed) + five tabs: Overview (next actions, team, schedule), Field (map, captures, notes, instructions), Office (files, drafting, research, deliverables and QA), Money (fee, change orders, invoices, payments, time), Conversation (messages and activity merged). Everything about the field lives on the map; one door in.
add: Deliverables and change orders on the page
nationwide: Tab tooltips, RPLS wording, drawing/legal stage names and checklist text are Starr's. Tab set should be configurable per firm type (boundary-only firm vs construction layout firm).
plans: docs/planning/in-progress/jobs-map-research-consolidation-2026-09-20.md (open: remove 'View field captures', add Research this Property button; 12 open questions)

name: Job stage pipeline, history and checklists
roles: any signed-in user (POST has no admin check)
purpose: Move a job through quote, research, fieldwork, drawing, legal, delivery, completed, with a history and per-stage checklist.

elements.name: STAGE_ORDER
elements.does: ['quote','research','fieldwork','drawing','legal','delivery','completed'] (stages/route.ts:11).

elements.name: cancelled / on_hold
elements.does: Accepted as stages in POST but not in STAGE_ORDER.

elements.name: STAGE_DATE_MAP
elements.does: Stamps date_accepted, date_started, date_fieldwork_complete, date_drawing_complete, date_legal_complete, date_delivered on first arrival only.

elements.name: Stage checklists
elements.does: Template items per stage (e.g. 'Title search completed', 'Final delivery sent to client') loaded on demand; ticked per item.

behaviours: Moves are allowed in both directions with no gate; a milestone date is written only once (route.ts:60-75).
Every move writes job_stages_history and an activity_log row, and notifies the job's team except the actor.
Checklists are advisory: a stage can be left with unticked items.
STAGE_CONFIG (labels, colours, emojis) is a second copy of the stage list in JobCard.tsx:37-47; mobile has a third in mobile/lib/db/schema.ts:512.
problems: 'cancelled' and 'on_hold' are stored in the same column as the pipeline stages, so putting a job on hold loses its place (it survives only in history); 'result' (won/lost/abandoned) is a second cancel mechanism.
No real QA step: 'legal' is the RPLS review, but there are no reviewer assignment, seal or approval states in the stage flow.
Billing is absent from the pipeline: 'completed' does not mean invoiced or paid.
The POST route does not check admin or job membership: any signed-in user can move any job.
Three copies of the stage vocabulary (route, JobCard, mobile schema) must be edited together.
No required-fields or required-checklist gates, so 'delivery' can be reached with no drawing and no deliverable.
rebuild: Separate three things now fused: production status (a short fixed set, see jobs.md), flags (on hold, blocked, cancelled with reason), and billing status. One shared constants module for web and mobile. Optional gates per firm (e.g. cannot reach Delivered without a sealed deliverable).
add: Per-firm stage names mapped onto fixed canonical states
nationwide: The seven stages, checklist text ('Corner records searched', 'Easements and ROW identified') and the 'legal' stage reflect Starr's boundary-survey workflow. Needs per-firm pipeline and checklist templates by survey type.

name: Job result (won / lost / abandoned) and cancellation
purpose: Record the pipeline outcome of a quote or job and why, for conversion reporting.

elements.name: Result control (job header)
elements.does: Sets won, lost or abandoned with a reason, or clears it.

elements.name: result_set_at stamp
elements.does: Set when a job becomes lost or abandoned if not already set (route.ts:370-373).

behaviours: Writes an audit_log entry per change.
Cancellation after starting work is recorded with a reason (JobMoneyPanel header notes the owner's request).
problems: Overlaps the 'cancelled' stage and the project 'cancelled' status: three ways to say 'this did not go ahead'.
'won' is set by hand on a job, but the lead already says 'accepted' and the stage moves past 'quote'. Win/loss belongs to the proposal, not the job.
rebuild: Win/loss lives on the proposal/opportunity. A started job can be Cancelled (with reason and a final invoice for work done). Remove 'won' as a manual job flag.
add: Competitor and price-gap capture on lost quotes
nationwide: No Starr-specific code; reporting vocabulary should be configurable.

name: Job financial tab: fee, payments, price history, time
purpose: Show bid, received and owed, record down payments and price changes, and log hours.

elements.name: Bid and final amount
elements.does: Click-to-edit quote_amount and final_amount; every change appends price history.

elements.name: Record payment
elements.does: Adds a job_payments row (type, amount, date).

elements.name: Reconcile warning
elements.does: Flags when jobs.amount_paid disagrees with the sum of job_payments.

elements.name: Time tracker
elements.does: Lists and adds hours per team member.

elements.name: Project-level payments
elements.does: A retainer or cheque against a whole project (project_payments).

behaviours: All arithmetic is in lib/jobs/money.ts; 'received' is the sum of payment rows, never jobs.amount_paid (money.ts:24-26, 119-123).
Project roll-ups are summed on read, never stored.
problems: Four overlapping money records: jobs.quote_amount (and leads.quote_amount mirror, lead_quotes versions), job_payments, jobs.amount_paid (legacy, still written by older paths), and invoices with their own payments. A payment recorded here does not touch an invoice and vice versa.
No invoice from the job: invoices/new can pick a job (invoices/new/page.tsx:302) but the job page has no 'Invoice this job' or billed-to-date view.
No change orders in the fee story, though change_orders exists (jobs.change-orders-api).
Fee model is one number: no lump sum vs hourly vs per-unit, no retainer, no phases or milestones billing.
Time entries show hours, not cost or margin against the fee.
rebuild: Job Money = Fee (from the accepted proposal) + Change orders = Contract value; Invoices and their payments as the only payment record; Time and expenses as cost; one panel: contract, billed, collected, unbilled, hours, margin. Retire jobs.amount_paid and job_payments as separate truth.
add: Create invoice from job (fixed, % complete, milestone, T&M)
Job profitability (hours x rate vs fee)
nationwide: Currency and tax assumptions are USD. Fee types and retainer practices vary; make them configurable.

name: Property panel (job site, parcel, lat/lon)
purpose: Where the property is: address with Google lookup, county, legal description, optional lat/lon, and the map button.

elements.name: Address box with suggestions
elements.does: Free text first, Google Places lookup second (PropertyPanel.tsx:288-297).

elements.name: County type-ahead
elements.does: Texas counties datalist only (line 330-331).

elements.name: Lat / Lon fields
elements.does: Manual coordinates the map opens on.

elements.name: Interactive map button
elements.does: Second copy of the map link, data-testid job-property-map (line 243-245).

elements.name: Geofence centroid and radius
elements.does: PATCH geofence route sets the site circle used to label GPS stops by job (radius at least 25 m).

behaviours: Edits are saved as one form instead of nine separate click-to-edits.
The owner asked the map button go to the property, not the default Belton view (line 241).
problems: Duplicate 'Interactive map' button also in the page action row.
County list is Texas only; a Louisiana parish or Oklahoma county cannot be chosen.
Geofence is a circle only; no parcel polygon, so GPS stop-to-job matching is rough for large rural tracts.
rebuild: A site card: address (lookup), parcel id(s) per state format, county/state from a national list, pin on the map. Parcel polygon from a county GIS layer where available; geofence derived from it.
add: State and county from a national list
nationwide: TexasCountyDatalist, 'rural Texas' comments, biasTexas autocomplete. Replace with state-aware county list and country bias per firm.

name: Job phase scheduler (Research / Field Work / Drawing and Deliverables)
purpose: Pick days and an assignee for three phases of a job; each lands on the org calendar with reminders.

elements.name: Phase rows (Research, Field Work, Drawing and Deliverables)
elements.does: Choose date(s) and assignee; POST /api/admin/schedule with event_type and job_id.

elements.name: Existing events list
elements.does: Reads schedule_events for this job and shows scheduled phases.

behaviours: Fires day-before and day-of reminders to the assignee.
Non-admins see only their own events in the schedule API; admins see all.
problems: Three phases here do not match the seven stages; there is no 'Review' or 'Delivery' phase to schedule.
Scheduling is per job one phase at a time: no crew-by-day view, no check that the assignee or the equipment is free (equipment has its own separate schedule).
No multi-person crew on a phase and no capacity check; schedule_events also carry PTO.
rebuild: Scheduling as a dispatch board: day x crew grid, drag jobs and phases onto party chiefs, vehicles and instruments, with conflict warnings (person on PTO, gear double-booked). The job's Schedule tab is a filtered view of that board.
add: Conflict detection across people, vehicles, gear
nationwide: Phase names are Starr's. Time zone is assumed per firm; check calendar sync defaults.

name: Job Files tab (standard folders, upload, send)

elements.name: Folder tree and file grid
elements.does: Standard folders plus custom folders; project files appear in the project mount.

elements.name: Upload (files, drag and drop)
elements.does: Chunked client upload; background upload helper; thumbnails made server side.

elements.name: Send
elements.does: Email a file to a contact (files/[id]/send).

elements.name: From research
elements.does: Attach a purchased or captured research document to the job.

behaviours: Reads EXIF GPS from uploaded photos and writes job_file_captures (files/route.ts:10, lib/jobs/exif-capture-server.ts).
A file keeps one id across the job explorer, project explorer and map (no copies).
problems: Bucket names are Starr-prefixed (starr-field-photos, -videos, -voice, -files) and are fixed constants in four routes.
Files can arrive from three paths (web upload, mobile storage_path, F5 capture) with different columns; the route normalises them but the schema is split.
No file versioning, no 'issued' lock on a drawing PDF that has been delivered.
rebuild: Keep the explorer. Add file status (working, issued, superseded) tied to deliverables so a delivered PDF is locked and versioned. Bucket names per tenant, not per product name.
add: Client portal share link per folder
Bulk download as zip with manifest
nationwide: Hard-coded bucket names; sample folder names assume Texas deed research. Folder set should be per-firm configurable.

name: Job to research link (Research packet, Start property research)
purpose: Give the crew the approved research packet on the job, and start a research project for the job.

elements.name: Research packet panel
elements.does: Four states (none, in progress, draft, approved) so a crew does not mistake empty for nothing; stores a copy for no-signal trucks.

elements.name: Start property research link
elements.does: Opens /admin/research?new=1&job=<id> inside the Files > Research folder; passes only the job id (jobs-page.tsx:1007-1012).

elements.name: Research documents (old panel)
elements.does: Fourteen-category add/expand/delete list from the original job workspace.

behaviours: Creating a research project does not start a run; a run is started separately inside research.
Address, county, parcel and documents do not travel to the research project.
problems: No 'Research this Property' button on the job header; the only door is buried in a folder and passes nothing but the job id (confirmed in the 2026-09-20 review).
Two research concepts remain: the old per-job research document list and the research platform's research_projects.
The word 'project' means a Starr project to jobs and a research run to research.
rebuild: One 'Research' action on the job that creates the research run prefilled with address, county, parcel and client, and returns a packet attached to the job with status. Retire the old document list.
add: Research status in the job header
nationwide: Research sources are Texas county-record and TexasFile oriented; every state needs its own adapter set.
plans: docs/planning/in-progress/jobs-map-research-consolidation-2026-09-20.md (open: Research this Property button, prefill fields)

name: Originating inquiry card (lead to job link)

elements.name: Card
elements.does: Reference number, reply count, office-note count, link to the lead. Renders nothing when the job has no origin lead.

behaviours: Looks up by jobs.origin_lead_id when present, else by the older leads.converted_job_id scan (origin-lead/route.ts:64).
problems: Two linking mechanisms (leads.converted_job_id and jobs.origin_lead_id) are both kept.
The card does not show the accepted quote or proposal the job should be priced from.

add: Accepted proposal and signature shown on the job
Marketing source for the job (feeds reporting)
nationwide: None specific.

name: Job team, equipment, instructions, notes, contacts, messages
purpose: Who is on the job, what gear is booked to it, the RPLS's written instructions, the note log, linked contacts, and the job conversation.

elements.name: Team panel
elements.does: Add or remove members with a role (job_team); the team receives stage-change notifications.

elements.name: Equipment list
elements.does: Manual job_equipment rows with checkout and return times.

elements.name: Instructions
elements.does: Text with [label](job-file:id) embeds resolved server side; broken links flagged; same on web and mobile.

add: Crew roles matched to licences and certifications
Customer and site contact with access notes (gate codes, landowner call-ahead)

behaviours: Sealing and issuing are actions so a plat cannot be marked final with nobody's name on it (route.ts:5-10).
problems: No admin screen calls this API, so nobody in the office can create, seal or issue a deliverable. The customer side does read it: the public portal page lists deliverables (app/portal/[token]/page.tsx:11), so the customer sees an empty list.
The job page edits a free-text jobs.deliverables description instead, so there are two concepts with the same name.
No link to the file that was sealed: file_url is a string, not a job_files id.
rebuild: Surface as a Deliverables panel on the job: list, add revision, 'Seal' (RPLS only, with seal number and signed PDF attached from job files), 'Issue' (recipient, method, date), receipt. Locks the file. Free-text jobs.deliverables becomes the scope line only.
add: RPLS review/QA queue of drafts awaiting seal
Digital seal/signature support per state rules
nationwide: Seal and signature rules, seal formats and e-seal allowances vary by state board; the seal number field should follow the firm's licence data.

name: Change orders (scope and fee changes) - API only
purpose: Record scope changes: description, signed amount, days added, with a customer approval link.

elements.name: GET ?jobId=
elements.does: Change orders in number order.

elements.name: POST
elements.does: Raise one.

elements.name: PATCH action send | approve | decline | void
elements.does: State changes; approval by public token with name, email and IP hash.

behaviours: Amount is signed so a reduction is just a negative change order.
problems: No admin UI raises or sends a change order. The customer approval page exists (app/change-order/[token]/page.tsx, API app/api/public/change-order/[token]/route.ts) and the portal lists them, but there is no way to create one from the job.
Not included in the job money roll-up (jobs.job-money), so approved changes do not move the contract value.
rebuild: Change-orders section on the job's Money tab: raise, send for e-signature, approve; approved amount adds to contract value and days to due date.
nationwide: None specific.

name: Jobs API group (CRUD, counts, resolve, activity, new, open)
roles: signed-in (many reads and a few writes)
purpose: All server operations for jobs and projects, including org scoping, numbering, soft delete, tab counts, type-ahead and the job reference resolver.

elements.name: jobs (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE)
elements.does: List with search and stage filter, create under a required project, update, soft-delete (30 days).

elements.name: counts
elements.does: Every tab's number in one request.

elements.name: resolve
elements.does: Type-ahead and verdict for a typed job reference (24-103) before filing against it.

elements.name: new and [id]/open
elements.does: Unread-job markers and last-viewed stamps.

elements.name: assignments
elements.does: Separate assignments CRUD (not described in the code read; purpose beyond job_team is unknown).

behaviours: supabaseAdmin is an org-scoped client: reads and updates are filtered and inserts stamped by org_id centrally (lib/saas/org-scope.ts).
Job number generation scans the org's jobs for the current year (route.ts:199-210).
JobRefPicker and resolve make 'which job is this?' consistent in pickers.
problems: Auth is inconsistent: stages POST and several reads only check signed-in, not job membership.
Sub-resources are split between query-string style (jobs/team?job_id=) and path style (jobs/[id]/notes); two conventions in one group.
jobs/field-data and jobs/[id]/field-data are different systems with near-identical names.
job_number generation reads all rows for the year; two simultaneous creates can race for the same number (only a unique index would stop it; not verified).
/api/admin/assignments purpose is not clear from its header: 'Assignments CRUD' only.
rebuild: Resource-style REST: /jobs/{id}/(team|files|stages|payments...) with per-job authorisation (member or admin), number allocated by a database sequence per org per year, an OpenAPI description so a second firm's integrations can be built.
nationwide: Job number format YYYY-NNN hard-coded in the route; per-firm format needed.

name: AI field assistant
purpose: A crew member types a surveying question (back-azimuth, closed traverse set up, IRS mileage rate) and gets a short answer.

elements.name: POST question
elements.does: Calls Claude with a surveying field-work system prompt and returns a concise answer.

behaviours: Moved from /api/admin/work-mode/assistant when Work Mode was retired (C0e); the text half only, voice is device-gated.
problems: No UI caller was found in the code read for this area; may be called from the mobile app or the floating assistant (not confirmed).
Not grounded in the job: it does not know the job's instructions, county or datum.
rebuild: Make it job-aware (job instructions, research packet, point list) and available from the field app; log questions for QA.
nationwide: Answers should be state-aware (state plane, local rules).

name: Starr Field mobile app (Expo)
purpose: The field crew's phone app: clock in on a job, capture photos, video, voice notes and points, notes, receipts, gear and vehicle, with offline queue and sync to the platform.

elements.name: Jobs tab
elements.does: Job list and search; job page with points, notes, files and previews; point detail (998 lines).

elements.name: Capture tab
elements.does: Create a point, then photos, video, voice (video player screen).

elements.name: Time tab
elements.does: Clock in/out with a job picker, time edits with history, vehicle picker.

elements.name: Gear tab
elements.does: Equipment, personal kit, truck contents, QR scanning.

elements.name: Money tab
elements.does: Receipt capture and review.

elements.name: Me tab
elements.does: Privacy, tracking consent, uploads queue, profile.

elements.name: Background location tracker
elements.does: 30 s or 50 m samples into local SQLite; synced when reception returns.

behaviours: Offline-first: PowerSync replays a local queue; uploads back off and retry (uploadQueue, uploadBackoff).
Biometric lock, push notifications, OTA updates.
Job stage vocabulary is a text column in the mobile schema (schema.ts:512), a third copy.
data: PowerSync / Supabase tables: jobs, field_data_points, field_media, job_files, job_time_entries, receipts, vehicles, equipment
problems: Mobile writes to field_data_points and field_media (zero rows today), while the office map reads job_map_points: the phone's captures do not reach the map.
No change of stage or QA from the phone; crew cannot mark field complete.
No instruction acknowledgement, no map view of the job's points (only a list).
Brand and bundle id are Starr-specific; the multi-tenant plan (MOBILE_MULTI_TENANT) is not shipped in this code.
The mobile app is large (11.5k lines in tabs alone) for a not yet launched product; the 2026-09-20 review calls the capture flow unused.
rebuild: Keep the offline architecture. Reduce the phone to three jobs: today's jobs (instructions, map, nav), capture (photo, video, voice, points straight to the job map), and time (clock-in with job and vehicle). Money and gear are secondary tabs behind permissions.
add: Map view with the job's points and the crew's position
Field-complete button that moves status and notifies the PM
Per-firm app branding (white label via EAS)
nationwide: App name 'Starr Field', bundle id com.starrsoftware.starrfield, tenant hosted storage buckets starr-field-*. Needs tenant config and white-label builds.
